newsitem.title: FRANCE: France calls for orderly transition in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France calls for orderly transition in Zaire.

text.p: France called on Thursday for an orderly transition towards elections in Zaire and questioned the democratic credentials of rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe, in an interview to be published on Saturday in the weekly Le Figaro-Magazine, cast doubts over the rebels' intentions to call elections.
"Who seriously thinks that the choice is between a tired dictator, Mr Mobutu, and a young, dynamic and modern democrat, Mr Kabila?" Juppe asked.
"When you hear (Kabila) say there won't be an election, that the people must first 'become sensitive to the doctrine', you can only worry about what it means."
Kabila on Thursday gave President Mobutu Sese Seko three days to start talks on standing down or face a fresh offensive on all fronts.

The French Foreign Ministry earlier called for an orderly transition of power in Zaire, signalling that Paris believes Mobutu is increasingly unlikely to halt the rebels. Kabila's forces now control about half the country.
"We want, as does the international community, an orderly and consensual transition towards national reconciliation and elections," Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said.
He said France, formerly a strong Mobutu's backer, believed it was essential to apply the U.N. peace plan agreed on February 18.
Doutriaux told reporters it was up to the people of Zaire to decide whether Mobutu, who has ruled for more than 31 years and is suffering from prostate cancer, remains in power.
"We strongly urge all Zairean authorities to search together for a peaceful way out of the current political crisis and devote their energies to the recovery of the country," he said.
"France will support without reservation all those who take this path with resolve."
Juppe dismissed reports that the successes of Kabila, a long-time opponent of Mobutu, were a setback for France. Paris has only in the past few days distanced itself from Mobutu.
"What is at stake is complex. Presenting the developments in Zaire as a setback for France would be an extraordinary simplification," he said.
Kabila's rebels captured the capital of the mineral-rich Shaba province, Lubumbashi, on Wednesday.
The capture of Lubumbashi was the most spectacular success of the six-month rebellion, which began when the rebels took up arms in October in a dispute over Zairean nationality for ethnic Tutsis.
